ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18968, effective Nov 1, 2024) as amended; Act on the Protection of Information and Communications; Commercial Act (Act No. 19000) for corporate registration; Enforcement Decree of the AML Act; Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (NTS) / District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of South Korea; no consular legalization required for Apostille Convention member states. For non-member states, consular legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the issuing country.
Hague Apostille by MOFA (South Korea) for use abroad; for foreign documents, apostille from the issuing country's competent authority, then accepted in South Korea without further legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney (이사회 결의서 / 위임장)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company's Board of Directors (notarized by a Korean notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, followed by Hague Apostille by MOFA (South Korea) for international use; for foreign-origin documents, apostille from the issuing country's competent authority.
Notarization by a Korean notary public, then Hague Apostille by MOFA (South Korea) if required for foreign filing; for foreign documents, apostille from the issuing country's competent authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in South Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by MOFA (South Korea) for use abroad; for foreign bank letters, apostille from the issuing country's competent authority.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean FIU's own list of designated persons and entities. Additionally, conduct enhanced due diligence (EDD) for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF, including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must be performed at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily), and upon any trigger event. Adverse media checks must cover corruption, money laundering, terrorism financing, and sanctions evasion. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. For high-risk jurisdictions, enhanced scrutiny and senior management approval are required. The protocol must align with the Korean AML Act and FATF Recommendations 10, 12, and 22.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS (Internet Court Registration Office) - Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) for registration, but an English trade name may be used as a secondary name. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names. For foreign entities, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name. The four-tier naming convention includes: (1) the corporate form (e.g., 유한회사, Yuhan Hoesa), (2) the distinctive name, (3) the business purpose, and (4) the registered office address. The name must not contain any prohibited tokens without prior approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, promulgated November 23, 1962, as amended), in particular Articles 287-2 through 287-74 addressing the Yuhan Hoesa (a private limited liability company), Article 288 requiring notarized Articles of Incorporation, and Article 331 governing registration of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court exercising jurisdiction over the registered office; for an office in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office; nationwide electronic filing through the Supreme Court Registration Information Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa, submitted together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, paid-in capital certificate, director and auditor consents, corporate seal registration form, and certified subscriber identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the total capital stated in the notarized Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid by bank deposit before the incorporation registration is filed. The capital subscription moneys must be deposited into a blocked escrow account in the name of the company or promoters, and withdrawal is not permitted until incorporation is registered. Non-monetary contributions must be supported by a statutory asset valuation report. An illustrative initial capital of KRW 10,000,000 corresponds to approximately USD 37 in registration duty and educational surtax.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF KOREA YUHANG HOESA. BE IT REMEMBERED THAT an organizational meeting of the Board of Directors of Korea Yuhang Hoesa, a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, was duly called and notice was validly served upon all directors. All directors were present either in person or by teleconference and unanimously waived formal notice in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The meeting was lawfully constituted and the Board adopted the following resolutions as corporate actions effective upon incorporation. RESOLVED, that the subscriptions to share capital as specified in the register of members and the Articles of Incorporation are acknowledged, ratified and accepted; that the issued shares are lawfully allotted to the subscribers; and that every subscriber shall fully pay the subscription amount into a blocked escrow bank account in Korea before the incorporation filing is accepted, with withdrawal to occur only after legal registration of the company has been completed. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office at the statutory address shown in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the authorized official venue and seat of the company, and that all official notices, legal process, tax correspondence and registry communications shall be served at that office. The directors are directed to file the registered office address, corporate seal and directors names with the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court. FURTHER RESOLVED, that a banking relationship be established with a reputable commercial bank at the jurisdiction of the registered office, and that the bank is authorized to open and maintain demand deposit accounts, foreign exchange transaction accounts for settlement of documentary letters of credit and documentary collections, usance receipts and export proceeds accounts. Any one of the two authorized signatories, namely the executive director and either the co-signing director or the auditor appointed in the following paragraph, may lawfully bind the company in banking matters. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as statutory officers of the company: a Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director who will act as the primary statutory representative of the company; a Compliance and Export Control Officer responsible for export trade licenses and customs declarations; and an Auditor if the company is required by law to have one, who shall supervise the directors, preserve capital and audit the annual financial statements. The Chief Executive Officer is authorized to execute all incorporation registration filings, tax registration, foreign trade registration, bank account forms and standard commercial agreements respecting raw cotton bales, synthetic yarns and related textile raw materials. FURTHER RESOLVED, that these resolutions are unconditional, immediately effective and binding upon all directors, promoters and officers, and that a certified copy be transmitted to any government authority or financial institution upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation and Validate Company Governance Terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public qualified in the district of the intended registered office of Korea Yuhang Hoesa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notarize the Articles of Incorporation before a notary public in the district in which the registered office is located. The object clause must precisely authorize international wholesale trade, distribution and brokerage of ginned raw cotton, synthetic yarns, textile fibers and allied raw materials falling under ISIC 4620 and NAICS 424590, and must prohibit unauthorized controlled goods or weapons. Present original passport or alien registration card of each individual subscriber, certified incorporation documents and power of attorney for legal person members, a registered seal impression card if a legal entity shareholder is involved, and the completed Articles in Korean. The notary must certify the date, the subscribers identities and signatures, and must issue a notarial certificate in the form required by Article 288. After notarization, the Articles may not be amended without a special resolution or court order.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean, single original and certified copies
Passport or Alien Registration Card of each individual subscriber
Certificate of incorporation, corporate seal certificate and power of attorney for any corporate shareholder
Registered seal impression card of a corporate promoter or corporate shareholder
Lease agreement or right-to-use document for the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries a subscriber's corporate capacity or any object clause, the founding members must correct the Articles by written resolution and execute the corrected Articles before the same notary. If the district court later rejects the notarial certificate, a supplementary certificate and amended application may be re-filed within the statutory correction window, usually two weeks from the notice of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-in Capital into Blocked Escrow Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean commercial bank branch in the jurisdiction of the registered office, and a foreign exchange bank designated under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for inbound non-resident subscriptions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish a blocked stock-issue escrow account with one of the Korean commercial banks where the company's registered office is located. Each subscriber shall deposit in full the amount of share capital subscribed or transfer the agreed non-monetary asset to the company or promoters; for inbound cross-border remittances, the remitting bank shall issue a foreign exchange remittance receipt and verify the source of wealth under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The bank shall mark the account as frozen or escrow, with withdrawal authorized only after the completion of incorporation registration or in proportion to refund in the event of failed incorporation. The bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued to the promoters must state the account number, depositor, date and confirmed blocked status. If a non-monetary contribution is used, attach a valuation certificate from a licensed appraiser and execute a contribution transfer before filing the registration application.
required_dossiers: Capital payment remittance record or bank certified receipt
Foreign exchange remittance receipt for inbound non-resident subscriptions
Valuation report for non-monetary contributions, if any
Identity documents for authorized bank signatories
Anti-money laundering source of funds declaration and bank KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account due to beneficial ownership or source of funds concerns, the applicants must promptly produce a corporate structure chart, trade contract and bank statement from the remitting institution. If incorporation fails, the promoters must apply to the bank for a pro-rata refund based on the failed registration notice and file an explanation with the registry if a subsequent application is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the Competent District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court exercising jurisdiction over the registered office, using the Supreme Court electronic registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application to the Commercial Registration Division of the competent District Court through the Supreme Court E-Registration system or by physical filing where required, annexing the notarized Articles, paid-in capital bank certificate, subscriber identification, directors statutory consents, auditor consent, specimen seal reports, and the application form stating the registered office and corporate purpose. The court registrar examines whether the object clauses are lawful, whether capital contribution is effectively paid, and whether statutory officers and the registered office comply with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, registration duty, education tax and court filing fees are paid online, the company is entered into the commercial register, and the court issues a certified Certificate of Registration. A corporate seal declaration is also registered at the same time.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital from the blocked escrow bank
Written acceptance of office signed by each director and auditor
Register of directors and statutory auditor details
Corporate seal registration form
Capital schedule and allotment table
Power of attorney for a licensed administrative or legal agent, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary order or query, a lawyer or licensed administrative agent must file a written response within the prescribed period, commonly two weeks, with corrected or supplemental documents. If the registrar dismisses the application, the applicant may appeal to the appellate court or re-file after curing the deficiency, preserving the original priority date where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company for Corporate Tax, Value-Added Tax and Local Income Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, submitted through Home Tax Service online portal or in person.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the period required after incorporation and before commencing business, file a business registration application under the Value-Added Tax Act with the jurisdictional District Tax Office of the National Tax Service, electronically through Home Tax Service or at the civil affairs window. The application must annex the corporate registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement of the registered office, certificate of capital deposit, and identification of the statutory representative. The tax officer will determine general taxpayer status, register the value-added tax account number, issue the Business Registration Certificate, and assign the employer registration number for withholding of local income tax and social contributions. For export trading, the registrant shall state the export-oriented zero-rated VAT nature and designate the bank account for export proceeds, while providing the customs clearance data required to support zero-rating of cotton bale sales.
required_dossiers: Corporate Registration Certificate issued by the District Court
Business registration application form
Lease contract or ownership certificate for the registered office
Certificate of paid-in capital and bank account statement
Corporate seal certificate
Passport or Korean ID of the statutory representative
Estimated value-added tax and corporate tax data for the first fiscal year
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a deficiency notice, the applicant shall file a corrected business registration application with the authentic lease, ownership certificate, and proof of actual site occupancy. A late business registration penalty may be avoided by submitting a written explanation showing that the delay was due to official processing or postal failure; if penalty is assessed, a tax tribunal objection may be filed within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Exporter Trade Registration and Customs Clearance Access
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single-window system, with advance authorization under the Foreign Trade Act for any strategic goods check by the Korea Strategic Trade Institute if required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a general trade business license under Article 19 of the Foreign Trade Act and register the company as an exporter with the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic single-window system, obtaining a digital certificate for export declarations. The application must attach the corporate business registration certificate, application form, directors passports, corporate bank account certificate, registered office lease and a statement of the planned export volume. Because ginned raw cotton classified under HS 5203 is not a strategic export commodity under the Public Notice on Trade of Strategic Goods, the application is expected to pass after simple documentary review. After approval, the entity must appoint a licensed customs broker or hire qualified internal customs clearance staff to submit pre-export declarations, maintain country-of-origin records, export invoices, packing lists, bills of lading and all documentary letter of credit papers required for the export of raw cotton bales under ISIC 4620.
required_dossiers: Application for General Trade Business License and Exporter Registration under the Foreign Trade Act
Company Business Registration Certificate
Corporate Registration Certificate
Representative and compliance officer identity documents
Foreign trade banking account certificate
Digital certificate application for UNI-PASS
Pro-forma export contract, commercial invoice and HS 5203 classification sheet for raw cotton bales
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Korea Customs Service rejects or suspends the exporter registration, the applicant must review the HS classification and submit a corrected application through UNI-PASS with customs broker endorsement. If a queried item relates to trade restrictions, the company shall file an application for non-strategic commodity confirmation with the Korea Strategic Trade Institute; if the application remains denied, an administrative appeal to the Customs Administration Dispute Committee may be filed within 90 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is a pure wholesale brokerage and export trader of raw cotton bales under ISIC 4620 and does not own a manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing facility. Any future operation of a physical warehouse or cotton bale compression plant would bring the company under the jurisdiction of the municipal building office, the Ministry of Environment, the National Fire Agency and the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no separate industrial operating license or manufacturing permit is required for the current business scope. The only mandatory operating approvals are the National Tax Service Business Registration Certificate and the Korea Customs Service exporter registration under the Foreign Trade Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment and its affiliated environmental agencies would become competent only if the company later establishes a cotton warehouse, compression facility or other physical plant exceeding the statutory EIA thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the current ISIC 4620 brokerage and export operation falls below all EIA activity categories and requires no environmental registration, environmental impact statement or pre-consultation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable today, as no discharge or emission source exists. If a warehousing or commodity handling facility is developed later, the operator must secure a wastewater discharge permit where daily wastewater generation exceeds the regulatory threshold, comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act limits for particulate and volatile organic compound emissions, and implement hazardous waste handling procedures under the Waste Management Act for contaminated cotton waste and packing materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to office-based brokerage and export trading operations. If the company later leases a cotton bale warehouse, it must obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire station under the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Fire-Fighting Systems, secure a structural load approval from the municipal building office for stacked cotton bales, and register the workplace with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, including work environment measurement for dust and fiber particulates under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), accessible through the Hometax national electronic tax portal at www.hometax.go.kr and Korean Customs UNI-PASS for export declarations
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that establishes or operates through a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must cause the Korean company to apply for business registration (Business Registration Number / Sa'eopja Deungrok) with the competent district tax office, or through Hometax using a tax representative where the foreign entity itself carries on a Korea-source VAT taxable business without a domestic place of business. The application must be made within 20 calendar days of commencing business, must include the constitutional documents, registered office evidence, foreign shareholder details, and identity documents of the tax representative where required, and results in a 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves as both the corporate taxpayer reference and VAT identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is classified under the Corporation Tax Act as a domestic corporation taxed on worldwide income; Korea does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity election. Foreign tax credit and controlled foreign corporation rules apply at the shareholder level but do not alter the entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold applies; any person, including a non-resident entity making taxable supplies in Korea, is statutorily required to register for VAT upon commencing business. Simplified taxable persons with annual taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000 remain registered but may use simplified VAT calculation and reporting rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (HomeTax e-tax invoices) are required for all VAT taxable supplies; taxpayers must issue and transmit e-tax invoices through the National Tax Service HomeTax API or EDI system within the statutory issuance period. Korea does not operate a continuous real-time transaction clearance or centralized digital stamping platform; anti-fraud control is achieved through mandatory e-tax invoice matching, periodic VAT return validation, and cash receipt issuance for B2C supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The zero rate applies to exported goods under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act where the Korean seller transfers ownership of the goods to a foreign purchaser and the goods are physically removed from Korea to a foreign destination under a valid Customs Act export declaration. The raw cotton bales must not be consumed, used, or supplied sub-divisionally within Korea prior to export, and the exporter must retain transport, customs, and settlement records evidencing the actual foreign delivery and foreign payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Declaration (Export Cargo Clearance Report / Suchool Shin-go Pil-jeung) filed through Korean Customs UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice signed by the Korean seller and the overseas buyer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing carriage to a foreign destination
Packing list and certificate of origin if required by the destination customs administration
Foreign exchange bank certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate proving receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Letter of Credit or documentary collection documents evidencing the contractual export payment terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to NTS verification of the export declaration, foreign exchange receipts, transport evidence, and payment reconciliation. Any false, unsubstantiated, or fictitious export zero-rating is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply and assessed to 10% VAT, plus additional tax for under-reporting, wrongful refund clawback, late-payment interest, and negligence or fraud penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including corporate fines and criminal liability where deliberate evasion is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF) as the external foreign exchange administration authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current-account operations, including trade in goods, services, and ordinary remittances; no prior approval is required for most current-account receipts and payments. Capital-account flows, however, are governed by a negative-list system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and require notification, reporting, or authorisation through an authorised foreign exchange bank or the Bank of Korea. Non-resident shareholders may inject equity and receive dividends, but profit remittances must be supported by audited or reviewed financial statements, a corporate dividend resolution, a tax withholding payment certificate, and, if applicable, a foreign-exchange purchase certificate issued by the remitting bank. For export activities, proceeds must be repatriated to Korea within the statutory period, but may be retained in foreign currency accounts; there is no mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW. Overall, Korea is assessed as an open yet administratively controlled jurisdiction, where banking counterparties must verify the transactional purpose and maintain a full paper trail for every cross-border payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio to KRW is required; Korean resident exporters may retain up to 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency deposit accounts held with an authorised domestic foreign exchange bank. However, the full amount of export proceeds must be received or repatriated into a Korean bank account within 5 months from the export declaration date. Any extension beyond 5 months requires the prior approval of the authorised foreign exchange bank, and all receipts must be reported to the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System through the collecting bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex are not licensed under the Korean Banking Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to act as foreign exchange banks in South Korea. They cannot provide KRW settlement accounts that are recognised by the BOK-Wire+ clearing system, and they cannot execute statutory FX transaction reporting with the Bank of Korea. A Korean LLC such as Yuhan Hoesa must maintain its principal treasury and foreign exchange accounts with a domestic Tier-1 authorised foreign exchange bank. EMIs may only function as auxiliary collect/payment tools outside Korea and cannot replace the local banking licence requirement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Korean LLC with non-resident ownership, at least one statutory director or signatory with material ownership should appear physically at the bank branch to complete the KYC interview. Some Korean banks allow a secure video-based KYC interview for low-risk commodity traders, but the documentary package must include apostilled or consular-notarised power-of-attorney documents if opening is completed by proxy. For the lowest friction onboarding, the company should schedule a single in-person visit of the statutory director to Seoul or Busan, bringing original corporate documents and UBO identification. Remote consular proxy opening is permissible in limited cases but is subject to the bank international compliance committee's written approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder structure with a newly formed Korean LLC using parent-company or nominee directors, making the ultimate beneficial ownership chain opaque.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation, full shareholder registry, beneficial ownership declaration for every natural person controlling 10% or more of the entity, six months of bank statements for each direct and indirect parent company, signed organisational chart, passport copies of all directors and UBOs, and a legal opinion from Korean counsel confirming there are no bearer shares, nominee arrangements, or trust structures obscuring control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags from international brokerage of raw cotton, including invoice values, weights, or grades that do not align with shipping and inspection documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction dossier for each trade lane: purchase order, proforma invoice, final commercial invoice, original bill of lading, independent weight and quality survey certificate from SGS, Intertek, or Cotlook-based price reference, export customs declaration, packing list, insurance certificate, and documentary evidence of payment or LC settlement matching the invoice amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and denied-party screening hits on counterparties, vessels, shipping agents, or intermediary banks in the cotton supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive compliance screening report from a reputable data provider such as Dow Jones, Refinitiv, or LexisNexis, with false-positive explanations, vessel IMO number and AIS tracking report, Denied Party List citations and adjudication, and a sworn board declaration that the goods will not be transshipped or re-exported to embargoed destinations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection and subsequent capital contributions arriving from a third-country pivot account or in fragmented tranches from a non-resident shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder bank statements evidencing legal provenance of wealth, confirmed foreign direct investment report or capital transaction declaration, board resolution approving the capital contribution, tax reference and corporate registration from the remitting jurisdiction, and a notarised undertaking that all future funding will be routed exclusively through the designated Korean capital escrow account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital contributions must be routed through SWIFT MT103 wires into the designated Korean foreign exchange bank. The remitter must cite the equity investment purpose and the FDI or capital transaction report number under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Upon receipt, the Korean bank matches the funds to the registered declaration, converts the foreign currency into KRW at the bank's market rate, credits the Capital Escrow Account, reports the transaction to the Bank of Korea Foreign Exchange Information System, and issues a capital verification certificate. No capital should be collected through offshore digital wallets, uncoded correspondent sweeps, or third-party settlement platforms.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for raw cotton procurement and brokerage settlements will be cleared through three channels: SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments, irrevocable commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) for sight or usance LC transactions, and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for risk-mitigated shipments. Each outward remittance must reference the underlying trade contract, commercial invoice, customs declaration, and transport document. The Korean bank will conduct a post-shipment audit to verify commodity consistency, quantity, price, and shipment route. All KRW/USD conversions for payment must be executed at the trade date rate with full audit trail, and speculative foreign exchange positions are prohibited.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Korean won deliverable forward contracts with a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank, strictly limited to the amount and maturity of an actual cotton purchase or sale contract

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for KRW/USD hedging may be permitted only where the bank approves the underlying trade exposure and where the hedge is classified as a current-account or documented trade-related transaction, subject to BOK and MOSF restrictions on offshore KRW NDF activity

Cross-currency swaps and vanilla FX options (call/put) are permissible when supported by documentary evidence of the underlying cross-border trade receivable or payable, and are forbidden when used for speculative or uncovered positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due on or before March 31 of the immediately following year. Entities required to obtain an independent external audit may e-file using the audited financial statements through April 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty equal to 10 percent of the tax payable, or 20 percent for repeated obstruction; late-payment interest charge computed at the statutory daily rate of approximately 0.022 percent on any unpaid tax; seizure and compulsory sale of corporate assets; administrative registration strike-off of the legal entity for sustained non-filing and loss of current address.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporation income tax surtax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Wetax electronic local tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable simultaneously with the national corporate income tax return; within three months after the fiscal year-end, with the same audited-entity extension to April 30 for calendar-year registrants.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local income tax surcharge of 10 percent of the unpaid tax for failure to file; additional 0.022 percent per-day late-payment interest; forced collection procedures, including real property and bank account seizure, pursued by the local government without a separate court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval by the members of the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records at the registered office; no governmental filing is separately required for a private non-listed limited liability company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Hold and memorialize the annual members' meeting within three months after the fiscal year-end, i.e. by March 31 for a calendar-year entity; unanimous written consent in lieu of a physical meeting is permissible under the Korean Commercial Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fixed monetary fine is imposed by a government filing agency, but failure to approve the financial statements forfeits the audited-entity tax extension, invalidates the auditor's required report, exposes directors to liability for losses attributable to the omission, and constitutes a red flag leading to NTS delinquency penalties and potential court-appointed inspection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements to the financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) on behalf of the Securities and Futures Commission, and made available to members and creditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where audit thresholds are met, the auditor must be appointed before the annual members' meeting; the audited financial statements must be finally approved at the annual meeting within three months after fiscal year-end and submitted to FSS within three weeks from the date of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor allows the Securities and Futures Commission to appoint an auditor at the company's cost; the company is subject to administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000; unaudited financial statements are deemed invalid for tax loss carry-forward and dividend distributions; serious cases are publicly announced and may be referred for criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise status and performance declaration (conditional on non-resident ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the relevant ministry under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an actual foreign investment transaction, the report must be filed within 30 days of the share subscription, transfer, disposal, or increase in the capital stock; the annual business-status report, if triggered, is due by March 31 following the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 5,000,000 for failure to submit the report; loss of protected foreign-investor status, revocation of tax incentives, and mandatory audit referral for deliberate concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Korean Act on External Audit of Joint Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to appoint an independent certified public accountant or audit firm if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, any of the following criteria is satisfied: (i) total assets are at least KRW 5 billion; (ii) the entity is part of a consolidated group in which a parent or controlling company is subject to external audit and the entity itself has assets of at least KRW 1 billion; (iii) the entity is classified as a public-interest entity because it has 500 or more regular employees or total assets equal to or greater than KRW 1 trillion; or (iv) the company's annual revenue is at least KRW 10 billion and it has at least 300 average employees, applying the Enforcement Decree's small-scale and semi-large company rules to limited companies. For this raw-cotton export brokerage, the decisive trigger is the KRW 5 billion total-asset threshold or a parent-group consolidated audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Unless the company elects to apply Korean Adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), the applicable statutory accounting framework for a private Yuhan Hoesa is Korean GAAP for small and medium-sized entities (SME K-GAAP), including the financial statements presentation, disclosure, and measurement requirements set out in the External Audit Act. If an external audit is required, the financial statements must be prepared in Korean Won, filed with the corporate income tax return, and presented to the Securities and Futures Commission via FSS, using either K-IFRS or K-GAAP consistently from year to year. For the purpose of this compliance matrix, the statutory books and underlying accounting records must be retained for a minimum of seven full tax years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a general annual UBO reporting return on every private limited company. The Yuhan Hoesa must instead maintain a current member register showing each member's name, address, contribution, and quota; transfers are effective only upon registration in this register. The National Tax Service annual corporate return serves as the no-change confirmation event. Whenever a non-resident member subscribes, acquires, transfers, or disposes of any membership quota, the entity must satisfy the 30-day reporting window under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act measured from the date the transfer is recorded in the member register. The company must also record the practical ultimate beneficial owner in its anti-money-laundering/KYC records with its transactional banks, and any refusal to disclose beneficial ownership creates a bank-de-risking event and a statutory ground for the financial institution to terminate the relationship.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Yuhan Hoesa member ledger)
Minute book including annual general meeting resolutions and written consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 1,500 per year for a Seoul-based registered office, corporate secretarial agency, and registered agent; provincial locations range from USD 500 to USD 1,000 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 for a simple single-entity Yuhan Hoesa export brokerage; USD 12,000 to USD 30,000 where group consolidated or parent-audited financial statements are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income surtax on the national CIT amount, producing a combined top marginal rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific incentive applies to raw cotton export brokerage. General Korea incentives: R&D tax credits up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditure; Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays for qualified high-tech foreign-invested enterprises (five-year exemption and 50% reduction for the following two years); job-creation credits; SME preferential 9% national rate on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; and possible municipal local tax reductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return for Each Fiscal Year filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal, together with the 10% Local Income Tax Surtax Return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with semi-annual corporate tax interim prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end the statutory deadline is March 31, extendable by one month if the return is prepared and signed by a certified tax accountant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Fiscal Year and Corporate Identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the fiscal year start and end dates, corporate registration number, head office address, and foreign shareholder identification fields.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Korean LLC, state each foreign shareholder's name, country of residence, ownership percentage, and beneficial ownership details. If the LLC has no domestic place of business, appoint a domestic tax representative for service of process; failure to do so renders notices ineffective and exposes the foreign shareholders to assessment risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile book income to the corporate tax base by adding non-deductible expenses, deducting tax-exempt income, applying special reserves, and subtracting qualifying loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct raw cotton brokerage commissions or service fees paid to foreign related parties unless the economic substance and transfer pricing documentation establish arm's-length character. Loss carryforwards are limited to qualifying losses incurred within the previous ten fiscal years. For export brokerage, recognize commission income when the underlying contract is performed; advance SWIFT or LC deposits must be deferred only if performance obligations remain open.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Computed Tax and Local Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive national CIT rates of 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24%, then calculate the 10% local income surtax on the national tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim a foreign-invested enterprise tax holiday only if the LLC holds written approval under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and maintains the qualifying business activity in Korea. A loss-making Korean LLC with continuous foreign ownership and no local payroll may be challenged under the GAAR as a treaty-shopping vehicle even if the Box 3 calculation is mathematically correct.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Foreign Tax Credit and Tax Treaty Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim credits for foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income such as offshore brokerage commissions and export-related service income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Tax Residency Certificate, foreign tax assessment documents, and a source-country income allocation. The foreign tax credit cannot exceed the Korean CIT attributable to the foreign-source income. Non-resident shareholders receiving dividends may not claim this corporate credit; treaty relief must be handled separately under the non-resident withholding procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Additional Taxes and Penalty Surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report late-payment interest, unfaithful return penalties, and transfer pricing adjustment surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If an international related-party transaction is adjusted by the NTS, include the corrected taxable income and pay the resulting additional tax with penalty surcharges before the audit closes. Voluntary correction under the Framework Act on National Taxes may reduce the penalty by 50%; deliberate concealment with cross-border shell companies escalates the matter to criminal tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Non-Resident Withholding and DTA Rate Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare dividends, interest, royalties, and other income paid to non-resident shareholders or foreign related parties during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold the statutory 22% on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties unless a reduced Double Tax Treaty rate has been accepted by the NTS. Attach the Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and proof that the recipient has no Korean permanent establishment. Failure to attach these documents prohibits the reduced treaty rate and may trigger withholding agent liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; underreporting attracts 10%; fraudulent concealment or false claims attract 20%; unfaithful returns with a tax due of zero still attract per-form flat penalties. Overdue tax accrues daily surcharges at approximately 0.022% per day. Criminal evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is punishable by imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to twenty times the evaded tax, with aggravated imprisonment potentially exceeding five years when the evaded amount is extraordinary.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% total statutory withholding on outbound dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident shareholder, composed of 20% national non-resident corporate income tax plus a 2% local income surtax, subject to DTA reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting the dividend, interest, or royalty payment, the beneficial owner must submit to the Korean withholding agent and NTS: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence country's competent authority; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is not an intermediary; (3) the statutory Application for Income Tax Reduction/Exemption under Tax Treaty; (4) shareholding period and ownership ratio evidence for dividend treaty rates; and (5) a principal purpose test substantiation showing the transaction was not designed primarily to obtain treaty benefits. The reduced DTA rate is applied only after the NTS accepts the application; otherwise the 22% statutory withholding applies and a refund must be pursued separately through the Korean international tax refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic statutory rate for interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10-15% and royalties to 10-15%, depending on the specific DTA and the nature of the industrial royalty. If the non-resident recipient has a Korean permanent establishment effectively connected to the income, treaty benefits are denied and the income is taxed on a net basis together with the Korean branch.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required if the Korean LLC has annual revenue of at least KRW 50 billion and international related-party transaction volume of at least KRW 5 billion. Master File is required if annual revenue is at least KRW 100 billion and international related-party transactions are at least KRW 50 billion. Country-by-Country Reporting applies when the ultimate parent group has consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion. A raw cotton export brokerage LLC below these thresholds must still maintain contemporaneous TP documentation sufficient to demonstrate the arm's-length nature of each intercompany commission or financing arrangement.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation filing, but substance is decisive. The NTS applies the statutory substance-over-form principle and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule to disregard entities lacking real offices, employees, contracts, books, bank accounts, and decision-making authority in Korea. For treaty benefits, Korea applies the BEPS Action 6 limitation-on-benefits and principal purpose analysis; the LLC must demonstrate its Core Income-Generating Activities for raw cotton export brokerage are genuinely performed in Korea, not by a foreign affiliate in a low-tax conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion through fraudulent export documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately issuing fictitious commission invoices, inflating raw cotton brokerage service values, or shifting profit to a related offshore entity through artificial contracts while the Korean LLC remains a bare shell with no employees, premises, contract negotiation files, or independent business supervision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3: imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to twenty times the evaded tax; Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-2 through 47-5 impose an additional 20% deficiency penalty plus daily late-payment interest; aggravated tax fraud thresholds may lead to imprisonment exceeding five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed fraudulent invoices or approved the sham contracts are jointly and severally liable under Korean tort and corporate law; under National Tax Collection Act Article 12 they may be designated secondary taxpayers and held personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax when corporate assets are insufficient; the NTS may issue a departure restriction travel ban against delinquent directors and criminal conviction disqualifies them from serving as company officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit outbound dividend, interest, or royalty withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident shareholder or related party without withholding the 22% statutory amount, or applying a discounted DTA rate without a Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership proof, and the tax treaty reduction application accepted by the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Income Tax Act Article 98 and Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-4 make the withholding agent liable for the unwithheld amount plus an additional 10% penalty; Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 4 criminalizes intentional non-withholding, carrying imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to twenty times the withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director and finance officer who execute the payment instruction are personally liable as withholding agents for the unremitted tax, with joint and several exposure to NTS enforcement; intentional non-withholding constitutes a direct criminal offense triggering personal arrest, asset seizure, departure restriction, and possible imprisonment of the responsible directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and treaty shopping lacking economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Korean Yuhan Hoesa solely as a re-invoicing conduit for raw cotton export proceeds, maintaining no actual commercial functions, physical office, personnel, or board activity in Korea, and relying on the Korean entity's name to claim treaty benefits or obtain tax preferences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may disregard the corporate entity under the substance-over-form doctrine and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 2 of the International Tax Adjustment Act; the result is re-characterization of all income to the real controlling shareholders with an additional 20% penalty on understated tax, interest, and denial of tax treaty benefits under the principal purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil where the company is an instrument for avoiding legal obligations; director and controlling shareholder assets are reached through Commercial Act representative-director liability and secondary taxpayer collection. Criminal prosecution for deliberate shell-company tax evasion may impose imprisonment, fines up to twenty times the avoided tax, travel bans, and disqualification of the directors from holding any future corporate management position.
